properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 13 at 10:57AM AKDT until October 16 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A stronger atmospheric river is expected to move over the panhandle
beginning early Thursday morning and continuing through at least
Friday morning. Multiple waves moving up will bring persistent
moderate to heavy rain for much of the southern half of the
panhandle. Past early Friday morning, additional periods of heavy
rain are possible, but confidence is moderate to low at this time.
Prolonged periods of moderate to heavy rain will produce significant
river rises with the potential for at least minor flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Southern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Ketchikan And Metlakatla.

* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals between early Thursday morning and late Friday
morning for the Ketchikan and Metlakatla area are currently
expected around 4 to 6 inches, with higher rain totals favoring
southern facing mountainsides. Highest rain rates are currently
expected during the late morning through evening timeframe on
Thursday, where rates could exceed 0.3 inches per hour.

If the additional heavy rain moves into the southern panhandle
late Friday morning and continue through Friday afternoon, up to
an additional 1.5 inches is possible. The chances of this to
occur are around 30% at this time.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 13 at 8:39AM PDT until October 13 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and elevated surf are expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding can be expected
near times of high tide.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM PDT this
afternoon. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 5 PM PDT
this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
around high tide at low-lying beach and harbor areas that is
uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is
possible. The risk for significant damage is very low. There
is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to peak around 7.2
feet this morning. The Beach Hazards Statement will likely be
extended into Thursday morning due to minor tidal overflow from
continued elevated tides and surf.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.description:
ESFGUM

This Hydrologic Outlook is for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan.

Invest 96W is still a broad, disorganized disturbance located about
300 miles north of Kosrae. Ensemble model guidance continues to show
a passage anywhere between south of Guam to north of Saipan as a
tropical storm or typhoon. Uncertainty is still high regarding
timing, location, and intensity, but the potential for locally heavy
rainfall and flooding continues to increase approaching this weekend.

This is expected to produce 5 to 8 inches of rainfall between
Saturday and Monday, with localized amounts up to 12 inches possible.

As showers are likely to persist, consistent rainfall is likely to
saturate the soils enough to increase chance for mudslides.

Residents on these islands need to closely monitor this developing
situation as flood watches, advisories and flash flood warnings could
be issued later this weekend.

If living near streams and rivers, prepare to move items away from
stream and river banks. Make sure storm drains nearby are not
clogged, especially If living at low-lying areas.

Invest 96W is currently rated as "Medium" by the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center, meaning tropical cyclone development is likely, but
beyond 24 hours. It's currently located west of Ujae near 9.3N
164.4E. It continues to slowly organize and strengthen north of
Kosrae/east-northest of Pohnpei.

Inflow into the developing disturbance will allow for locally heavy
rainfall to develop, with over 1 inch per hour rain rates probable
from time to time. Rainfall totals will likely be 2 to 5 inches
tonight through Thursday, with locally higher amounts possible.
Winds will also increase as 96W strengthens, and at least isolated
wind gusts to 30 knots are possible with any heavy shower or
thunderstorm that develops.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues. Also keep up to date with the latest
information from your local emergency management agency.
